page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-800s-amd is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, offering 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled to provide 8 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32 MB of Level 3 cache, 64 GB of system RAM providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and 800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not included, and networking connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark metrics reflect the dedicated x86_64 architecture with notable memory and single-threaded performance. Single-core results place in the top percentiles, including a stress-ng score of 3132.97 in the top 10% and a Geekbench single-core score of 1996.0 in the top 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, achieving 228.44 GB/sec for uncached reads and 156.49 GB/sec for writes, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 2876.37. Overall multi-core throughput aligns with median cloud benchmarks, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 20591.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9998.0 across its 8 vCPUs. Compute-intensive language processing tasks show limitations, with 7B model prompt ingestion averaging 24.79 tokens per second.

With 64 GB of memory and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, the voc-m-8c-64gb-800s-amd delivers a cost-efficient resource footprint for memory-bound and I/O-intensive workloads without incurring costs for separate detached block volumes or underutilized GPU compute. The server profile is suitable for in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, intermediate data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput web backends.

The instance demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, registering 228.44 GB/sec on uncached reads and 156.49 GB/sec on writes, alongside upper-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng and Geekbench. Multi-core performance and web serving metrics track closely with cloud median averages, while complex language model inference is constrained by core counts and instruction sets. Given its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation and bundled NVMe capacity, the instance offers balanced density and qualitative operational cost efficiency for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data processing pipelines, and general business applications requiring generous memory capacity.
